requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST use
the current workspace source at book-render time and explicitly identify its
contents as current workspace source notes.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.current` has no structural obligation, and it has no implementation edges or review roots. Each clause describes observable behavior:

- "MUST use the current workspace source at book-render time" says which data the rendered view reflects and when. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface. Any implementation that reads the workspace source during rendering meets it. A precomputed or cached snapshot would fail it by showing stale output, which is a behavioral difference. So this is not a structural choice.
- "explicitly identify its contents as current workspace source notes" is a labelling requirement on the rendered output. Any code or template that emits the label satisfies it. Finding the code that produces the label would not make it structural.
- The cited parent, `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes`, sets only context. It says each listed file gives access to a notes view identifying its workspace-relative path, which is also observable output.

The obligations are therefore behavioral, and tests cover them. No implementation evidence is needed.

behavioral: The subject has two behavioral obligations. First, the notes view must use the current workspace source at book-render time. Second, it must explicitly identify its contents as current workspace source notes.

The marked test is `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[each_render_reads_current_notes_and_keeps_recorded_reviews_without_writing]`. It covers both obligations.

- **Current source at render time:** The test renders once with the original note text. It then rewrites `code.rs` to say "Updated platform" and renders again. It asserts that the new render contains "Updated platform explanation.". It also asserts that the part of the output before "Review:" no longer contains "Original platform explanation.". An implementation that cached or reused stale notes would fail both assertions.
- **Explicit identification:** The test asserts that the rendered content contains "Current workspace source notes". The `pages` implementation emits this text as its "**Current workspace source notes**, read at book-render time" label.

The assertions are relevant to the requirement and enforce it, so I found no gap.
